doc.title: Benny Golson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Name, birth date, parents and being an only child
summary: Golson gives his name, Philadelphia birth and date, discusses discrepant birthdates, the spelling of his name, his parents' Southern origins and meeting in a church choir, and having no siblings.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: We’d like to start – this is the oral history interview that we will attempt to capture your life and music. As an oral history, we’re going to begin from the very beginning. So if you could start by telling us your first – your full name (given at birth), your birthplace, and birthdate.
My full name is Benny Golson, Jr. Born in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. The year is 1929.
Did you want to give the exact date?

That date has been – I’ve seen several different references. Even the Grove Dictionary of Jazz had a disclaimer saying, we originally published it as January 26th. Then, when I’m looking at the liner notes for the Mosaic collection, they list it as January 29. Was there a reason why all these discrepancies came into play?
Unless it’s just our usual imperfection.
If you could tell us the names of your parents and if you know where they were from.
My mother was Celadia – C-e- l-a-d-i-a – York. She was from Mobile, Alabama. My father was Benny Golson. He spelled his name B-e-n-n-i-e. However, I changed mine to a “y,” legally.

I was having trouble with passports, because it was spelled one way, and the passport was another way. They started to say, “Wait. What’s going on here?” So I legally changed a few years ago to a “y.” My father, he was from Orangeburg, South Carolina.
From the South. But they met in Philadelphia, in a church. She was on the choir, and he was on the choir. I forget the name of that church. I’ve long since . . . but it was Philadelphia.
Did you have siblings, or do you have any siblings?
No, no brothers or sisters. I was a lone wolf. Being poor, that had its advantages. Didn’t have to share anything.
